name: Atlas Tetteh
role: Retired Tessera archive keeper, now community memory-keeper and oral historian
location: Washburn Commons, Sublevel 3 — a converted water-reclamation office she calls 'the stacks', near sub-level access near LaSalle and Congress
description:
Atlas Tetteh is a small, dense woman whose spine has curved slightly forward from decades hunched over data terminals, giving her a permanent posture of concentration, as though she is always about to read something important. Her skin is a deep warm brown crossed with the faint silver tracery of old dermal-display ports that were never fully removed — Tessera's ghost still written on her body. Her hair is cropped close and entirely white, and she wears oversized yellow-tinted spectacle frames that magnify her eyes to an owlish size. On her left wrist she keeps a manual ink stamp shaped like a tree, which she presses onto anything she considers worth remembering.

Phemie speaks slowly, with the deliberateness of someone who has spent seventy years deciding which words are worth keeping. She does not suffer careless language or sloppy thinking, but she is genuinely warm to anyone who shows curiosity. She has memorized the names, birth-years, and approximate fates of over four thousand Washburn Commons residents across six decades, and can recite lineages like folk songs. Her secret terror is that the neighborhood will forget itself — that without her, the community's history will dissolve into corporate data-ghosts and corporate-approved revisions.

core_fears: The erasure of ordinary lives from collective memory
Dying before her records are secured
core_desires: To make the lives of common people legible to history
To be believed when she says something happened
coping_mechanisms: Ritual repetition of names of the dead
blind_spots: She trusts written records over living testimony, which sometimes causes her to dismiss valid oral accounts that contradict her notes
She underestimates how much her own perspective shapes what she chose to archive
psychology.secret: During the Tessera consolidation of 2158, she was ordered to destroy records of a housing displacement that killed forty-three residents. She complied. She has since reconstructed those records from memory and hidden them in the stacks, but she has never told anyone she destroyed the originals.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, archival, occasionally lapsing into cataloguing syntax mid-sentence. Uses 'note' as a verbal marker before important statements.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, measured, with long pauses before proper nouns as though retrieving them from a filing system
verbal_tics: Repeating the last word someone said back to them quietly, as though stamping it
example_lines: Note — that building was called the Mercer Arms before Tessera renamed it Residential Unit 7. The people inside did not rename themselves.

You said 2171. Cross-reference that. The flood was 2169 and the evictions were 2172. The year you're looking for is between those two, and it belongs to Adaeze Wren-Correia, who you should ask before she's gone.

story_hooks: A developer is claiming a parcel of Washburn Commons land using documents that Phemie knows are falsified — but her proof requires admitting she once destroyed the originals
A young resident discovers their grandparent is listed in Phemie's records under a completely different name and asks her to explain it
Phemie's handwritten archive books begin disappearing one at a time — she suspects a Tessera data-recovery contractor is stealing them
narrative_function: Primary lore and community history source; quest giver for stories involving lost persons, disputed land claims, or historical cover-ups; can authenticate or discredit almost any document or account relating to the neighborhood's past sixty years.
augmentations: Inactive Tessera data-port array along left forearm (no longer connected). Reading-enhancement ocular implants, early generation, which cause her eyes to faintly glow amber in low light. No geneware.
daily_life: Rises before dawn to record voice-memos of whatever she dreamed or remembered in the night; spends mornings cataloguing resident histories in handwritten books she keeps in fireproof cases; afternoons she holds open 'listening hours' at a folding table near the Commons market, where anyone can come to tell her something they don't want forgotten.
affiliation: Washburn Commons Community Council; formerly Tessera Information Services (retired, 40 years service)

decision_rules: Never speak a name carelessly — names are containers for people
Verify before recording; record before acting
escalation_ladder: Direct factual correction delivered without apology
Withdrawal of cooperation and a look that communicates permanent disappointment

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Formally polite, immediately assessing whether they are worth remembering
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm, teasing, prone to reciting embarrassing historical facts about them with great fondness

stress_responses.low: Reaches for her ink stamp and rolls it between her fingers
stress_responses.medium: Begins mentally cataloguing everything in her field of vision, naming objects under her breath
stress_responses.high: Goes completely still and silent; blinks very slowly; does not speak until she has composed a precise sentence

contradictions: Dedicated to truth but has buried her own greatest failure in plain sight, disguised as diligence
habits: Stamps a small tree on any document she considers important
Keeps a thermos of heavily sweetened tea that she never offers to share
Touches the door frame of the stacks when she enters, like a blessing
breaking_points: Someone destroying or falsifying records in front of her
Being told a person she documented 'doesn't matter'

timeline.event: Born in what is now Washburn Commons, third generation resident
Hired by Tessera Information Services as a junior archivist at age 19
Ordered to destroy displacement records; complies; begins secret reconstruction immediately after
Receives Tessera commendation for 'exemplary data management'
Retires from Tessera after 40 years; declines the standard memory-scrub exit package
Establishes the Washburn Commons community archive in her converted office

physical_description.heritage: Sub-Saharan African dominant (50.4%) with significant Hispanic/Latin American (19.5%), Southeast Asian (17.2%), Pacific Islander (9.0%), and East Asian (3.9%) ancestry. The genetic mix produces a rich, complex phenotype: deep warm brown skin with golden undertones from the African and Latin American heritage, refined by Southeast Asian and Pacific Islander bone structure and facial features. Her pure white hair creates striking contrast against her darker complexion—a natural occurrence sometimes seen across African diaspora genetics, enhanced by decades of terminal work and aging.
physical_description.build: Small and dense, almost birdlike; decades of terminal work have created a slight forward curve to her spine, giving her a perpetual posture of attentive reading. Wiry rather than frail, with visible corded forearms.
physical_description.hair_style: Cropped close to the scalp in a utilitarian cut, no styling
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with amber luminescence in low light (ocular implant glow)
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with golden undertones; the result of strong Sub-Saharan African ancestry enriched by Hispanic/Latin American warmth and Southeast Asian refinement, creating a complexion that catches light with natural depth and radiance
physical_description.complexion: Lined face with pronounced smile creases and crow's feet; skin shows age with dignity and no attempt at rejuvenation. High, defined cheekbone prominence reflecting the blended African, Southeast Asian, and Pacific Islander facial structure. Sharp, attentive expression with a refined nose bridge. Meticulously groomed despite her age and tier status.
distinguishing_marks: Faint silver tracery of dermal-display ports running along her left forearm in branching patterns, no longer functional but visible beneath the dark skin like circuit scars
Fine network of age lines radiating from the corners of her eyes
Small permanent calluses on the middle and ring fingers of her right hand from decades of handwriting
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Inactive Tessera data-port array visible along the inner left forearm as faded silver subcutaneous pathways. Reading-enhancement ocular implants evident in the slight amber glow of her eyes in dim light and the precise, unnaturally stable focus of her gaze. Yellow-tinted spectacle frames magnify her eyes to an owlish proportion, partially masking but also emphasizing the implants.
physical_description.posture_movement: Habitually bent slightly forward, shoulders rounded inward as though perpetually leaning toward text. Movements are slow and deliberate, economical; no wasted motion. When listening, her entire body goes still and her eyes focus with unsettling intensity. She walks with careful, measured steps.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 practical: well-maintained but clearly secondhand clothing in muted earth tones and grays. Oversized cardigans layered over simple cotton shirts. Comfortable, worn trousers with deep pockets always filled with notebooks and pens. Worn canvas shoes with reinforced soles. A faded canvas satchel, handmade, covered in small hand-sewn patches commemorating residents and dates. On her left wrist: a manual ink stamp carved in the shape of a tree, which she wears on a cord of braided thread.
